raw.query: SELECT source_path, n_images, sm_clock_mhz, mean_ms FROM collector_encoder_fn WHERE engine='sdpa' AND n_images=64 ORDER BY source_path;  -- plus: SELECT source_path, metric, value_text FROM collector_scalar WHERE source_path LIKE '%fn_silicon%' AND metric IN ('clocks_locked','clocks_mhz_observed','note')
raw.observed: Author's own 'unlocked' collection (fn_silicon) ran at SM 2385-2392 MHz (clocks_locked=false but effectively pinned ~2400), vs 'locked' anchor_sdpa_locked2400 at 2400 MHz. Matched N=64 latencies: 511.26 ms vs 511.68 ms = 0.08% diff; ledger confirms stable-clock re-run reproduces the unlocked mean 'to the digit' (511.68 vs 511.23, 0.09%).
raw.claimed: ≈17% faster (initial collection at unlocked clocks vs final locked dataset)
raw.evidence: DB's only unlocked-vs-locked clock pair records both runs at ~2400 MHz with latencies within 0.1%; the stored 'unlocked' run was not at unlocked boost (2385-2392 vs 2407 target, capped), so no 17% gap exists in the data.
raw.fix: Correct the claim: the stored 'unlocked' collection was already pinned near 2400 MHz and matches the locked run within 0.1%. To assert 17%, cite a genuine unlocked-boost collection (up to 3105 MHz) with its measured wall-clock/throughput, or restate as a clock-ceiling scaling note rather than a measured 17% gap.
